title: Storage Days Held Past the Notice Period — Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Deficiency Quotes
content:
**Cap on billed storage.** For storage carried into a deficiency quote on a Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract, and only for such storage, the billed storage days on the most recent storage charge (the first one listed where two share a date) are capped when the company held the vehicle longer than the notice period before selling it. The storage on the billed days above the cap is credited against the deficiency figure at the daily storage fee for the tier. The days from the notice of intent to sell to the sale are counted in calendar days from the notice mailing date recorded on the contract to the sale date recorded on the contract.

| State notice period recorded on the contract | Days from the notice of intent to sell to the sale | Cap on billed storage days |
|---|---|---|
| Longer than 15 days (the company minimum notice period) | more than the state period | the state period |
| 15 days or shorter | more than 15 days | 15 days, the company minimum |
| Any | not more than the period above | no cap; nothing credited |
| Any — no notice of intent to sell on record | — | no cap; nothing credited |
| Any — no storage charge on record | — | no cap; nothing credited |

Credit: the billed storage days less the cap, never below zero, times the daily storage fee for the tier.

**Hypothetical case.** State notice period 10 days, notice of intent to sell mailed and the sale held 24 days later, most recent storage charge billing 22 days: the cap is 15 days, and 7 days of storage are credited at the daily storage fee for the tier.

### Storage billed when the vehicle leaves the lot

Storage is billed only for days the vehicle is on the storage lot, and each such day only once. The lot days of an involuntary recovery whose most recent condition report is dated after the repossession date run from the day after that lot-intake date, the nights before it being the agency's holding, billed on its transport charge and never as storage; the lot days of a voluntary surrender run from the repossession date itself; any other lot days run from the day after the repossession date. A lot day up to and including the latest statement date on which a storage charge was billed is billed by that charge, whatever the charge came to, and a lot day collected in a redemption figure or a reinstatement amount or counted into a deficiency quote is not billed again. Every other lot day through the release or sale date is charged at the daily storage fee once the free days are used up, and it is billed when the vehicle leaves the lot. The free days for that charge — the charge billed when the vehicle leaves the lot — follow the recovery history: an involuntary recovery of a contract that shows an earlier reinstatement payment has none, a voluntary surrender of a contract that shows no reinstatement payment has the surrender free days of 7, and any other recovery has the free days for the tier, in each case less any free days an earlier storage charge for the same repossession already set against its stored days.
